samples.summary: Always materializing `lineAffinity` on the caret changes local selection highlight rendering beyond the issue's scope. Shift-selection anchors come from `cursor.position` (text-editor.ts:2948 and :2981, `anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? this.cursor.position`). Previously that position usually carried no affinity, so `buildRects` applied its documented asymmetric default (selection.ts:260: range start reads `'forward'`). Now the caret always stamps a concrete value (usually `'backward'`), so a keyboard-started selection whose anchor sits on a wrap boundary paints its start on the previous visual line — the zero-width-sliver case docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:84-87 says the asymmetric default exists to avoid. The doc's new paragraph asserts absent affinity is 'reserved for endpoints from other producers' but never acknowledges that caret-derived range starts changed reading; it also brushes that note's Non-Goal 'Changing the visual caret rendering behavior' (line 60).
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:2948 `const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos;` / :2981 `?? this.cursor.position;` with cursor.ts:55 `lineAffinity: affinity ?? pos.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'` and selection.ts:260 `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward';`

samples.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` declares `lineAffinity: 'forward' | 'backward' | undefined` as a required positional parameter whose documented use is 'omit it'. Because required params follow it, it cannot be omitted; callers must pass `undefined` explicitly. Making it optional (moved last) or an options object would match the documented intent.
samples.evidence: peer-cursor.ts:95-111 '@param lineAffinity — … Omit it to use the affinity the position itself carries' on a required positional parameter

verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out in the tree. cursor.ts:26 and cursor.ts:52-56 always materialize `lineAffinity` (defaulting to 'backward') onto `Cursor.position`. Keyboard shift-selection anchors are taken straight from that caret position at text-editor.ts:2893, :2948, :2981, :3000 and :3015 (with `pos = this.cursor.position` at text-editor.ts:2629), and selection.ts:115-181 (`normalizeRange`) forwards anchor/focus untouched into `buildRects`, whose start default at selection.ts:260 (`start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`) is therefore never exercised for caret-derived starts. The doc at docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:83-87 explicitly justifies that asymmetric default as avoiding a zero-width sliver on the line above, and line 60 lists "Changing the visual caret rendering behavior" as a Non-Goal, so the scope/Non-Goal argument is grounded in real text. I cannot refute on any named ground: the code is present exactly as described, no guard elsewhere strips anchor affinity or makes the path unreachable, and a Non-Goal/scope-creep + design-doc-discipline complaint is inside the design-fit lane. Confidence is low only because the doc's new paragraph (lines 96-98) does partially document the caret-always-materializes decision and the practical rendering delta may be a zero-width rect, so the blocking judgement is arguable — but that uncertainty correctly keeps the finding.
